description: Server integration surface: the agent-aware alert engine edits + rule-schema widening + payload attribution, the fleet event/state surface feeding the engine with global maintenance and agent-offline alerting, the shared control-status HTTP mapper, the unified /api/agents REST routes, the server-mode health router + mode field, the WsHub log-relay hook with validated agentId, the logger redaction keys, the server boot wiring, and the in-process agent<->server integration test. This is the convergence of the agent (FEAT-002) and server-core (FEAT-003) layers into a working server runtime behind MODE=server. Depends on FEAT-001/002/003. Covers plan.md items 13-20 and 22. Maps to design sections 5, 6, 7 and FR-3/FR-5/FR-6/FR-8/FR-9 with AC-28, AC-30..AC-33, AC-51..AC-56, AC-59.
steps: Edit src/alerts/engine.ts for agent-awareness (composite key = `${agentId}/${name}`, split on the LAST '/'): extend ruleTargets(rule,key) to match '*' | full key | bare name-part; extend targetNames(rule,present) to expand a bare name to every present key whose name-part matches and pass through composite selectors; add an injected `resolveAgent(key) => { agentId?, agentAlias?, name }` (constructor option, default = identity resolver returning { name: key }) and have buildPayload split the key, attach OPTIONAL agentId/agentAlias, and prefix summary/title with alias-or-id ONLY when agentId is present (processName stays the bare name). The default resolver keeps existing constructor callers compiling and standalone output byte-identical.

Edit src/config/alertRules.ts: widen processSelector to z.union([z.literal('*'), processNameRule, compositeTargetRule]) where compositeTargetRule = z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}\/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$/). This is a superset so existing rule files still validate.
Edit src/alerts/channels/types.ts: add optional agentId?: string and agentAlias?: string to AlertPayload.

Extend src/alerts/engine.test.ts and src/config/alertRules.test.ts: matcher matches '*' / full agentId/name / bare name against a composite-keyed present set; two agents with a same-named process do NOT share a cooldown or cross-trigger; a bare rule fires on that name across all agents; the standalone identity resolver yields payloads with agentId/agentAlias ABSENT and unprefixed summary/title (byte-identical to current output); the rule schema accepts agentId/name, still accepts bare names and '*', and rejects a two-slash/empty-part target.

Create src/server/fleetEvents.ts: re-emit fleet frames with composite keys; implement the server AlertStateHub/AlertErrorWindows over the FleetRegistry (processNames() -> agentId/name across online agents; getProcess/sustainedAbove/countInWindow/restartsInWindow parse the composite key by splitting on the last '/' and dispatch to the owning agent's store); build the resolveAgent closure over the registry + AliasStore (nameHint seeds the initial alias only when none stored; operator alias always wins); emit a single cooldown-gated agent-offline alert (synthetic rule id __agent_offline__ keyed by agentId) on disconnect and suppress per-process crash alerts for an orderly disconnect; expose a single global MaintenanceState holder read by getMaintenance(). Add src/server/fleetEvents.test.ts (cross-agent evaluation over the composite surface; payload carries agentId+agentAlias via the resolver; global maintenance suppresses across all agents; single agent-offline alert, no per-process crash alerts on orderly disconnect).

Create src/api/routes/controlStatus.ts: `statusForControlCode(code: string): number` -> 409 for PM2_UNAVAILABLE/AGENT_OFFLINE/AGENT_TIMEOUT, 404 for AGENT_NOT_FOUND, 400 for VALIDATION, 502 for PM2_ERROR/default. Leave src/api/routes/processes.ts#sendControlResult UNCHANGED (binary 409/502). Add src/api/routes/controlStatus.test.ts (asserts the mapping + a separate assertion that the standalone sendControlResult stays binary 409/502).

Create src/api/routes/agents.ts + a `FleetDeps` surface (narrow, injectable like StateDeps): mount under /api/agents behind the existing human auth. Routes: GET /api/agents (list keyed by the LIVE registry — pre-seeded aliases for never-connected ids are NOT listed; each row { id, alias, online, meta, pm2Connected, processCount, lastSeen }), GET /:id (404 AGENT_NOT_FOUND), GET /:id/processes, GET /:id/processes/:name/metrics?sinceMs, GET /:id/processes/:name/logs?lines&stream&q&level (returns { name, lines } from the live ring; { name, lines: [] } when no subscription), GET /:id/errors, POST /:id/processes/:name/{start|stop|restart|reload|delete} (routeControl -> statusForControlCode; ok non-create -> 200), POST /:id/processes (create: server-side createProcess.safeParse({ body: opts }) BEFORE routing; 201 ONLY when result.ok===true, every failure via statusForControlCode), PUT /:id/alias { alias } (aliasSchema -> AliasStore.set -> { id, alias }, 400 on invalid). Validate :id with agentIdSchema and :name with processNameSchema. Add src/api/routes/agents.test.ts (list keyed by registry, pre-seeded alias not listed; per-agent reads/control via a fake FleetDeps; PUT alias validation + persistence; routed-control HTTP mapping 409/404/400/502; server-side { body } create validation before routing, create 201 only on ok; human auth still enforced).

Edit src/api/routes/system.ts: add `mode` to the standalone health payload (otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged); add `createServerHealthRouter(deps)` returning { status:'ok', mode:'server', maintenance:<global holder.active>, agents:{ total, online }, version, uptimeMs } with NO pm2Connected, reading the global MaintenanceState + a FleetRegistry summary (no StateDeps). Do NOT mount /api/system/status in server mode. Extend src/api/routes/system.test.ts (standalone health gains mode:'standalone' and is otherwise unchanged; createServerHealthRouter returns the server shape with no pm2Connected via a fake registry summary + global maintenance holder).

Edit src/ws/hub.ts: add an optional `relay` hook (FleetLogRelay) and an optional `agentId` on log:subscribe. When agentId is present: FIRST validate it with agentIdSchema and process with processNameSchema and streams against ('out'|'err')[] BEFORE any registry lookup or upstream frame; on failure return the existing { type:'error', code:'BAD_MESSAGE' } frame and touch neither the relay nor the registry; on success register the client with the relay (ref-counted per (agentId,process)), send log:subscribe upstream, push arriving log:line as the existing { type:'log', ... } frame, and on client disconnect/log:unsubscribe send log:unsubscribe upstream. When agentId is ABSENT keep the existing local fan-out path byte-identical (no new validation, no relay). Extend src/ws/hub.test.ts (valid agentId reaches the relay hook + triggers an upstream subscribe; malformed agentId [bad charset, '/', __proto__, non-string] -> BAD_MESSAGE and the spy relay records zero calls; no agentId -> existing local fan-out unchanged).

Edit src/core/logger.ts: add AGENT_TOKEN, AGENT_TOKENS, SERVER_URL to REDACTED_KEYS, and correct the stale module docstring ('shallow + one level nested') to describe the real full-depth recursion plus the single array edge (arrays are not key-redacted). Extend src/core/logger.test.ts ({AGENT_TOKEN}, {AGENT_TOKENS}, {dial:{url:'wss://h/agent?token=secret'}}, and a depth>=2 {a:{b:{AGENT_TOKEN}}} all redact; a case documenting {list:[{AGENT_TOKEN}]} is NOT key-redacted).

Create src/boot/server.ts: `bootstrapServer(config)`. Wire the human createServer (mount createServerHealthRouter instead of createHealthRouter; do NOT mount /api/system/status) + WsHub with the relay hook + AgentGateway + FleetRegistry + AliasStore (load() at boot) + the global MaintenanceState holder + the agent-aware AlertEngine (fed from fleetEvents with the injected resolveAgent) + the /api/agents router (FleetDeps over the registry/alias store). Reuse the existing /api/maintenance routes to toggle the global state. Native TLS when both TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE are set (https.createServer reading the files; WsHub/AgentGateway attach identically via noServer), else reverse-proxy termination (plain http). buildAgentAuthConfig(cfg) supplies the gateway tokens. Install graceful shutdown. Edit src/index.ts so bootstrap() calls bootstrapServer() for MODE==='server'. Add src/boot/server.test.ts (fakes) asserting the agents routes + gateway are mounted and health reports mode:'server'.

Create src/server/integration.test.ts (AC-59): an in-process agent<->server over loopback ws (real sockets, no TLS) using an injected fakePm2Client on the agent side and the human WsHub on the server side — register handshake -> server receives the snapshot -> a routed control command round-trips (routeControl -> agent executes against the fake -> correlated response -> HTTP result mapped by statusForControlCode) -> a log subscribe relays a log:line to a human client -> unsubscribe stops it.
acceptance_criteria: `npm test` passes all existing suites plus the new/extended engine, alertRules, fleetEvents, controlStatus, agents-routes, system (health), hub (relay), logger (redaction), server-boot, and integration tests.

The alert engine evaluates across all agents with composite keys, attributes alerts to the originating agent id/alias, keeps global maintenance and cooldown global, and emits exactly one agent-offline alert on orderly disconnect while suppressing per-process crash alerts (AC-30/31/32/33); the standalone identity resolver keeps standalone payloads byte-identical.

The unified /api/agents surface lists agents, exposes per-agent processes/metrics/errors/logs, routes control with correlation and correct HTTP status mapping, and updates aliases — all behind the unchanged human auth (AC-25/26/27/28/34/53).
Server-mode health reports mode:'server' with an agents summary and no pm2Connected; standalone health only gains the additive mode field (AC backward-compat).
The WsHub relay validates agentId before any registry/upstream access and leaves the standalone path byte-identical (AC-28, NFR-1); agent tokens and wss URLs are redacted from logs (AC-51).
TLS is verified by default with a clearly-marked insecure toggle, supporting both reverse-proxy and native TLS (AC-54/55/56).
The in-process integration test exercises handshake + routed control + log relay round-trip (AC-59).
findings:
Implemented and green: npm run build clean, npm test 327/327 (283 preserved from FEAT-003 + 44 new/extended for FEAT-004). Exact exported names/paths for FEAT-005 (dashboard + docs) to wire:

src/alerts/engine.ts (agent-aware): new exports `AgentInfo { agentId?, agentAlias?, name }`, `ResolveAgent = (key)=>AgentInfo`, `identityResolveAgent(key)` (standalone default -> { name:key }), `bareName(key)` (part after LAST '/'), `AGENT_OFFLINE_RULE_ID = '__agent_offline__'`. AlertEngineOptions gained optional `resolveAgent` (defaults to identityResolveAgent so existing callers compile and standalone output is BYTE-IDENTICAL: no agentId/agentAlias, no summary/title prefix, processName = bare name). ruleTargets(rule,key) matches '*' | full composite key | bare name-part; targetNames(rule,present) expands a bare name to every present key with that name-part and passes composite selectors through. buildPayload splits via resolveAgent, prefixes summary/title with `[alias-or-id] ` ONLY when agentId is present, processName stays bare. New public `engine.emitAgentOffline(agentId, alias?)`: fires ONE cooldown-gated (synthetic rule __agent_offline__, cooldown keyed by agentId) agent-offline alert through the SAME global cooldown + maintenance holder + all enabled channels; payload { ruleId:'__agent_offline__', processName:'(agent)', agentId, agentAlias?, severity:'warning' }.

src/alerts/channels/types.ts: AlertPayload gained optional agentId?/agentAlias? (populated only in server mode).

src/config/alertRules.ts: processSelector widened to z.union([literal('*'), processNameRule, compositeTargetRule]) where compositeTargetRule = /^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}\/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$/ (a strict two-part join; rejects two-slash/empty-part). Superset — existing rule files still validate.

src/api/routes/controlStatus.ts: `statusForControlCode(code): number` -> 409 PM2_UNAVAILABLE/AGENT_OFFLINE/AGENT_TIMEOUT, 404 AGENT_NOT_FOUND, 400 VALIDATION, 502 PM2_ERROR/default. NOTE: FEAT-002 findings cited AGENT_TIMEOUT->504; reconciled to 409 per design §4 (the authoritative statusForControlCode table). src/api/routes/processes.ts#sendControlResult left UNCHANGED (binary 409/502).

src/api/routes/agents.ts: `createAgentsRouter({ fleet: FleetDeps, schemas, now })` mounted at /api/agents behind human auth. Exports `FleetDeps` (listAgents/getAgent/agentProcesses/agentMetrics/agentLogs/agentErrors/routeControl/routeCreate/setAlias), `AgentListRow { id, alias, online, meta, pm2Connected, processCount, lastSeen }`, `AgentDetail extends AgentListRow { processes }`, `AgentLogLine`. Routes: GET / (live rows), GET /:id (404 AGENT_NOT_FOUND), GET /:id/processes, /:id/processes/:name/metrics?sinceMs, /:id/processes/:name/logs (returns {name,lines} from the live ring, [] when nothing streaming), /:id/errors?name, POST /:id/processes/:name/{start|stop|restart|reload|delete} (routeControl->statusForControlCode, ok->200), POST /:id/processes (server-side createProcess.safeParse({ body }) BEFORE routing; 201 ONLY when result.ok===true, every failure via statusForControlCode), PUT /:id/alias { alias } (aliasSchema -> setAlias -> { id, alias }; 400 on invalid or AliasValidationError). :id validated by agentIdSchema, :name by processNameSchema.

src/api/routes/system.ts: createHealthRouter now adds `mode:'standalone'` (otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged). New `createServerHealthRouter(deps: ServerHealthDeps { maintenance: MaintenanceHolder, registry: FleetSummary { size, onlineCount() }, version, startedAt, now })` -> { status:'ok', mode:'server', maintenance:<holder.active>, agents:{ total, online }, version, uptimeMs } with NO pm2Connected. /api/system/status NOT mounted in server mode.

src/ws/hub.ts: WsHubOptions gained optional `relay?: FleetLogRelay`. Exports `FleetLogRelay { subscribeLogs(agentId,process,streams,client):boolean; unsubscribeLogs(agentId,process,client) }`, `RelayLogClient { deliver(line: RelayLogLine) }`, `RelayLogLine`. log:subscribe/log:unsubscribe with an agentId: FIRST validate agentId (agentIdSchema from src/protocol/shapes.ts) + process (processNameSchema) BEFORE any relay/registry touch; on failure the existing { type:'error', code:'BAD_MESSAGE' } frame and ZERO relay calls; on success register a ref-counted-per-socket RelayLogClient and relayed log:line is pushed as the existing { type:'log', agentId, process, stream, line, level, ts } frame. No agentId -> existing local fan-out, byte-identical. Client disconnect tears down all its relay subs.

src/core/logger.ts: REDACTED_KEYS += AGENT_TOKEN, AGENT_TOKENS, SERVER_URL. Module docstring corrected to describe FULL-DEPTH recursion + the single array edge (arrays are not key-redacted).

src/server/fleetEvents.ts: `GlobalMaintenanceState(now?)` { getMaintenance(): {active,until?,reason?} with lazy expiry; setMaintenance({active,durationMin?,reason?}) } — the ONE global holder the /api/maintenance route + engine read. `FleetStateHub(registry, maintenance)` and `FleetErrorWindows(registry)` implement AlertStateHub/AlertErrorWindows over composite agentId/name keys (split on last '/', dispatch to the owning entry's MetricsStore/ErrorTracker; processNames() = agentId/name across ONLINE agents). `buildResolveAgent(registry, aliases): ResolveAgent` — operator alias (AliasStore.get) wins; else AGENT_NAME via meta.nameHint; else bare id. `FleetAlertBridge({ registry, aliases, engine, events })` subscribes registry agent:online/offline, bridges each entry's per-agent events (process:transition/error:captured/metrics:tick) onto the fleet MonitorEvents with composite keys, and on offline fires engine.emitAgentOffline(id, alias) (no fabricated per-process crash alerts). REQUIRED a tiny additive change to src/server/registry.ts#onMetrics: it now also `entry.events.emit('metrics:tick', [...entry.processes.values()])` so the fleet engine's sampled (cpu/mem) rules run; no registry test observed metrics:tick on the entry bus so all FEAT-003 tests stay green.

src/boot/server.ts: `bootstrapServer(config, logger)` wires GlobalMaintenanceState + FleetRegistry + AliasStore(load) + agent-aware AlertEngine (FleetStateHub/FleetErrorWindows/buildResolveAgent) + FleetAlertBridge + WsHub(relay hook over registry.subscribe/unsubscribeLogs; SAME client identity for ref-count) + AgentGateway(buildAgentAuthConfig(config).tokens, wsPath=AGENT_WS_PATH). Native TLS when BOTH TLS_CERT_FILE/TLS_KEY_FILE set (https.createServer reading the files), else plain http (reverse-proxy termination). Exports `buildServerApp(deps)` (server-mode express app: server health unauthenticated, then human-auth + /api/maintenance [global holder] + /api/alerts [fleet engine] + /api/agents; /api/system/status NOT mounted) and `buildFleetDeps(registry, aliases): FleetDeps` (list keyed by LIVE registry — pre-seeded-only aliases NOT listed). Graceful shutdown closes wsHub/gateway/bridge/engine/server. src/index.ts MODE dispatch now calls bootstrapServer for MODE==='server'.

src/server/integration.test.ts (AC-59): in-process agent<->server over loopback ws (real sockets, no TLS) using injected FakePm2Client on the agent + AgentGateway/FleetRegistry on the server — register handshake lands online with the snapshot, a routed control round-trips (routeControl -> agent executes against the fake -> correlated response -> statusForControl 200; unknown process -> 502), and a log subscribe relays a line to a HumanLogClient while unsubscribe stops it.

Standalone (MODE unset) stays byte-identical: engine default resolver is identity (no agent fields/prefix), the no-agentId WS path is unchanged, health only gains the additive `mode` field, and all new code is server-only. No new runtime dependency (uses existing ws/zod/express). PM2 import site untouched.
